15780.description: &+lThis chamber is a war room located high within the guard tower of IceCrag Castle. The walls are lined with large wooden racks that hold various scrolls and rolled-up parchment maps depicting the surrounding landscape and strategic points of interest. A long, sturdy table made from oak stands at the center of the room, covered in additional charts and notes scattered about, indicating recent planning sessions. The floor is cold underfoot, likely due to a constant draft blowing through gaps between stones near the ceiling, hinting at an unsealed section or narrow slit high above for ventilation or defense. Iron braziers placed along the walls emit a dim &+yglow&N &+lbut do little to warm the chill air that fills the space.&N&+W
15780.brief: a war room high in the guard tower, maps and a cold draught

41180.name: A Ring of Ancient Oaks
41180.description: &+gThe thick trunks of oaks and birches grow close together here, and the ground between them is rich and loamy, thick with ferns and blackberry. But the trees to the &+ynorth&+g stand apart from the rest &+G- nine old oaks in a circle, their roots lifting a ring of turf that no bramble has crossed. &+WToadstools&+g crowd the inside of it. The air over the ring shivers like heat off a road, and the birdsong of the wood does not carry into it.&N
41180.brief: The Evermeet end of the faerie ring (links.json, 2026-08-08). Overridden so the crossing is findable: without prose naming the ring and the north exit, a player has no reason to walk into what the map draws as more forest.

77455.description: The narrow dirt path winds through dense undergrowth, barely visible beneath a canopy of oak and duskwood trees that block much of the sunlight. The ground is uneven with small stones and clumps of grass peeking through the earth, softened by fallen leaves and damp moss. Several patches show signs of recent use, with deeper imprints where hooves or boots have pressed into the soil. Twisted roots protrude from the earth at intervals, some partially covered by decaying branches that litter the path. The air is thick with the scent of wet earth and rotting wood, occasionally interrupted by the distant sound of a bird calling through the dense foliage.

77461.description: The trail here marks the edge where woods give way to open ground, winding between tall oak trees that stand like sentinels with their rough bark and sprawling branches. The air is thick with the scent of damp earth and decaying leaves, mingling with the faint fragrance of duskwood sap clinging to the breeze. Fallen logs lie scattered about, some partially covered by a carpet of moss and small wildflowers in various stages of bloom. Twisted roots emerge from the soil like ancient bridges, crossing the narrow path where they have been worn smooth by countless footsteps. The occasional rustle of unseen creatures moving through dense undergrowth adds to the sense of life hidden just beyond sight.

77462.description: The trail winds through clumps of thick brush and dense undergrowth, barely visible beneath a canopy of oak and duskwood trees that block much of the sunlight. The ground is soft with fallen leaves and needle-like fragments from nearby evergreens, crunching slightly underfoot. Twisted roots protrude from the earth at intervals, some partially covered by decaying branches that litter the path. Scrub bushes and thorny vines weave together, creating a natural barrier that seems to shift and grow with every passing moment. The air is heavy with the scent of fungi growing on damp tree trunks and the faint rustle of small creatures moving just beyond reach.

Fallen branches litter the ground around the tree's massive roots, their bark weathered and grey, while twisted roots jut out from the earth like ancient bones. The faint rustle of unseen creatures moving through underbrush adds a note of tension amidst the dense foliage.

77474.description: The ground gives way to patches of wet earth and boggy water, creating an uneven terrain where footprints quickly fill with dark, murky liquid. Dense clumps of brush and thorny vines weave together, blocking much of the sparse light that filters through the thick canopy above. The air is heavy with the scent of damp soil and decaying leaves mixed with the sharp tang of peat and moss. Fallen branches litter the ground, their bark weathered and grey, while twisted roots jut out from the earth like ancient bones. Small ripples disturb the surface of the bog water, hinting at unseen creatures moving just beneath the murky surface.

77475.description: The dense canopy overhead blocks much of the sky, leaving the forest floor dim and cool. The air is heavy with the scent of damp earth and pine needles. Ancient pines tower around, their trunks gnarled and twisted by countless winters. Fallen branches litter the ground, their bark weathered to a silvery grey, while twisted roots jut out from the soil like ancient bones. A narrow path winds through this stand of trees, with small pools of water collecting in the hollows where leaves and needles have formed soft carpets beneath the pines. The occasional soft rustle of unseen creatures moving through underbrush adds to the atmosphere of quiet tension.

77553.description: A thin film of moisture clings to the rough stone of the cliff face above. Brown water stains streak down the rock, tracing paths carved by countless rains over many years. A tangled curtain of hanging moss obscures much of the ceiling, its tendrils dripping onto the stagnant pool below. Several submerged logs float just beneath the surface of the dark water, their branches festooned with a sickly green algae. The air hangs heavy with the smell of damp earth and decaying wood. Scattered across the murky depths are pieces of broken stone; they appear to be parts of what was once paving. A few gnarled roots extend from the cliff face, clutching at the stones and snagging on passing debris.

Realms atmosphere carried entirely by physical detail: what has grown, rotted, sunk, been broken or been left behind. This room: Underneath the Overhang of an Easternly Cliff (Water).

77554.description: The stagnant water of the bog stretches out in every direction, reflecting a leaden sky. A network of dark channels weaves between the skeletal remains of trees, their trunks submerged to halfway. Here and there, a bloated bubble rises from the surface, popping with a soft hiss that fades quickly into the hum of insects. The air hangs thick with the smell of decay, mingling with a faint sweetness. Several grey stone markers jut from the water at irregular intervals; most are worn smooth by the relentless encroachment of the swamp. A crumbling brick structure half-submerged in the blackness rises to one side, covered in clinging moss and algae. Fragments of what appear to be ornate metalwork protrude from beneath a fallen tree trunk nearby.
77554.brief: The Stump Bog, in the Forgotten Realms: a drowned wood along the River Dessarin — black standing water, rotted stumps, and a decrepit cemetery slowly going under. Realms atmosphere carried entirely by physical detail: what has grown, rotted, sunk, been broken or been left behind. This room: The Stump Bog (Water).

77555.description: The surface water reflects the grey sky with no clear distinction between them. A thicket of thorny brush presses close on all sides, its tangled branches slick with moisture and draped in clinging tendrils of moss. The air hangs heavy with the scent of decay, a combination of stagnant water and rotting wood that stings the nostrils. Beneath the surface, a submerged root system writhes like pale serpents. Several large, half-submerged tree stumps stand sentinel across the area, their surfaces coated in a dark, algae bloom. A rusted metal clasp lies tangled among the roots at one's feet; it clearly once held something together. Further out, occasional fragments of broken stone are visible just below the water line.

Realms atmosphere carried entirely by physical detail: what has grown, rotted, sunk, been broken or been left behind. This room: Near a Thicket of Brush (Water).

77556.description: The standing water reflects the grey sky above with unsettling clarity. Thick reeds choke a large portion of the surface, their brown stalks swaying in an unseen current. Half-submerged tree stumps jut from the water at odd angles, slick with algae and draped with weeping moss. A crumbling stone marker leans precariously against one stump, its inscription long since obscured by grime and decay. The air hangs heavy with the scent of stagnant water and rotting wood, almost palpable on the tongue. Several rotted wooden frames lie half-buried in the muddy bottom, hinting at structures once present. Patches of dark silt accumulate around the bases of the stumps, soft underfoot. A tangle of thorny vines clings to a larger, tilted stump, blocking any view beyond.

77557.description: The surface of the water here is nearly black with decay. A thicket of thorny brush presses close on the far side of the standing water, its branches heavily laden with grey moss. Beneath the still surface, remnants of stone markers jut upwards like broken teeth; they are coated in a slick film of algae and grime. A single crow perches atop one such marker, occasionally letting out a mournful caw that hangs heavy in the humid air. The smell of wet earth and rotting leaves permeates everything, overlaid with a sharper tang of stagnant water. Twisted roots emerge from the black depths, forming an impossible network just below the surface. Here and there, scattered amongst the wreckage, small clusters of pale fungi cling to submerged timbers.

77558.description: The black water lies still and reflects a sky choked with grey clouds. A dense mat of algae carpets the surface, punctuated by the dark silhouettes of submerged tree trunks. The air hangs heavy with the smell of decaying leaves and stagnant water, clinging to the throat. Twisted roots claw out from the banks, coated in slick moss and glistening under the weak light. Several crumbling stone markers jut just above the water line, their inscriptions long since worn away. A thick layer of mud sucks at any disturbance near the edge, releasing a puff of foul-smelling gas. Patches of pale fungi cling to the rotting wood, casting an unsettling glow. Scattered amongst the stumps and debris are fragments of what once might have been ornate stone carvings.

77559.description: A thick layer of peat dusts the ground here where it gives way to drier soil. Rotting timbers and broken planks lie scattered about; remnants of a long-abandoned dock, perhaps. The smell of stagnant water hangs heavy in the air, mixing with a sharper scent of decaying leaf litter. A tangle of withered vines clings to several fallen tree trunks sunk knee deep into black water. Skeletal branches poke from the surface as if reaching for something just beyond grasp. Patches of coarse grass grow stubbornly amidst the decaying wood and muck. Further in, the dark pools of the bog begin, choked with shadow and the silence that comes with drowning.

77560.description: Black water fills the spaces between the gnarled roots of long-dead trees. Thick tangles of algae coat the surface of the stagnant pool here, reflecting a dull grey light from above. Several weathered headstones lie partially submerged near the northern edge; their inscriptions are worn and illegible with age. A scattering of broken flagstones rests on the muddy bottom visible in places between the dark water lilies. The air hangs heavy and damp, carrying the cloying scent of decay and wet earth. Rotting wood crunches beneath any surface disturbance, releasing a puff of black silt into the brackish depths. Further west a cluster of skeletal trees rise from the gloom; their branches snag on the occasional scrap of tattered cloth caught in their grip.

77561.description: Black water fills this depression in the land, mirroring the overcast sky above. Thick, clinging moss drapes across the submerged roots of countless trees, softening their form. A scattering of flat stones lies partially exposed, slick with algae and coated with a fine layer of silt. The air hangs heavy with the smell of decaying wood and stagnant water. Several crumbling headstones are visible just beneath the surface, their carved inscriptions blurred by years of submersion. Rotted planks jut from the blackness alongside skeletal remains of what seems to have been a fence at one time. 77628.description: The water is murky here, barely reaching past the shins and clinging to silt-covered boots. A rocky cliff face looms above, slick with algae and streaked with dark stains of runoff that smell faintly of decay. Tangled roots descend from the cliff's edge, submerged in the still water and covered with a film of green slime. Several gnarled branches protrude from the depths, their tips coated with clinging weeds and fragments of what may have once been leaves. A collection of small stones lies at the base of the cliff, displaced by something heavy pushing against them long ago. The air hangs thick and still, carrying the scent of stagnant water and rotting wood from deeper in the bog. Debris drifts lazily across the surface: a fragment of carved bone and a section of rusted metal.

77629.description: The surface of the black water is slick with algal bloom and still as a mirror in this area of the bog. A thick layer of decaying leaves coats the exposed roots of several ancient trees that have fallen into the swamp. Rotted wooden posts, once part of fencing or perhaps grave markers, jut from the dark water at odd angles. The air hangs heavy with the smell of stagnant water and the sharp scent of mildew clinging to submerged timber. A scattering of shattered stone fragments lies half-submerged around the base of a large, moss-covered stump. Long strands of grey willow hang low over the water, occasionally brushing the surface. Further out across the swamp, gnarled tree trunks rise from the gloom like broken teeth.

77630.description: The black water stretches out before a low rise of saturated earth. A thick mat of algae coats the surface, trapping floating debris like broken branches and fallen leaves. Several weathered wooden posts jut from the bog's dark depths, remnants of what were once fence lines or markers along a path. The air hangs heavy with the scent of decay and stagnant water, acrid in the nostrils. Clusters of hardy reeds cling to the northern edge of the landmass, their seed heads drooping under the weight of moisture. A scattering of skeletal shrubs are strewn across the low ground surrounding the water's edge; their gnarled limbs reach upward as if attempting escape. Further out, submerged tree stumps form a ghostly forest just below the surface.

77631.description: The water here is black and still, reflecting the grey sky like a sheet of oiled stone. A thick mat of algae coats the surface of the bog, clinging to the exposed roots of drowned trees. Several weather-beaten headstones jut from the murky depths, their inscriptions blurred by years of moss growth and persistent dampness. Rotting wood forms an island of stumps nearby; dark brown shapes pressed tight together like a morbid puzzle. A network of tangled reeds scrapes against unseen obstacles just below the surface. The smell is overwhelmingly earthy; a mix of decay and stagnant water hangs heavy in the air. A lone, rusted iron band encircles one submerged headstone, slowly separating from its stone base.

77632.description: Dark water fills this area of the bog, stagnant and smelling of decay. Twisted roots, submerged just below the surface, snag at unseen things beneath the inky blackness. A thick layer of duckweed carpets much of the open water, occasionally broken by a cluster of brown reeds. Several long-rotted headstones, barely visible through the murk, jut from the water's surface like broken teeth; moss coats their weathered surfaces. A crumbling stone wall stands here and there at odd angles, mostly collapsed into the water. The trunks of old trees rise everywhere as black stumps above the waterline, most covered in thick green algae. Above, the grey sky is barely visible through a canopy of drooping branches laced with Spanish moss.

77633.description: Murky water fills the area around the base of a massive stump. Thick green algae clings to its submerged roots and slick surface, releasing a pungent smell into the still air. Several broken headstones lie half-submerged in the shallow water nearby, their inscriptions obscured by layers of moss. Twisted branches from long-dead trees reach up from the dark depths. A few scattered leaves drift lazily across the surface of the stagnant pool. The rotting wood gives off a damp, earthy scent that mixes with the smell of decay. Deeper down, tangled roots and unseen debris obscure the bottom of the water.

77634.description: The hill crests abruptly here. Thick, clinging mud cakes the boots as one ascends; its smell is faintly sour. A tangle of thorny vines claws at exposed skin and clothing along the slope's edge. Below, the bog stretches out - a flat expanse of stagnant black water punctuated by the skeletal remains of trees. The skeletal branches of submerged trunks reach upward like grasping fingers from the depths of the murky water. Closer to hand, several stunted willow saplings struggle in the saturated earth, their leaves drooping with the weight of moisture. A scattering of grey stones are clustered near one side; they appear to be part of a collapsed wall or foundation. The air hangs heavy and still, broken only by the drone of unseen insects.

77635.description: The ground is soft with mud and decaying leaves in this forgotten place. Numerous stone markers lean at odd angles amongst the thick reeds crowding the edge of the black water. A few of the stones are half sunk into the mire, their inscriptions illegible beneath layers of algae. The air hangs heavy with the smell of damp earth, rotting wood, and something vaguely metallic. Twisted roots of long-dead trees clutch at the stone markers like skeletal fingers. A scattering of small, bleached bones lies near a fallen marker bearing a faded carving of a harp. Dark water laps persistently against the base of each stone; the surface is covered in a slick film.

77636.description: The ground gives way slightly with each step across this forgotten cemetery. Moss clings thickly to many of the crumbling headstones, obscuring faded inscriptions beneath its green mantle. A dense fog hangs low above the stagnant water pooling amongst the graves, smelling sharply of decay and wet earth. Several stones have entirely sunk into the mire, leaving only fragments jutting from the surface like broken teeth. Twisted roots from long-dead trees claw across some of the markers, pulling them further down into the swamp. A thick blanket of algae floats on the standing water, undisturbed by any breeze. The air carries the persistent hum of insects and a distant croaking sound. An ancient wrought iron fence circles this place, but many posts have collapsed or broken away, swallowed by the bog.

77637.description: The ground here gives way with each step into the black water and mud. Many weathered stones jut from the mire, their inscriptions blurred by years of rain and moss growth; some have sunk so far they are almost completely submerged. A tangle of thorny vines covers most of the grave markers, bearing clusters of dark purple berries that smell sickly sweet in the humid air. The boles of ancient trees-long since drowned-rise from the water like skeletal fingers surrounding the clearing. Several toppled headstones lie fractured, a few face up showing faint images of angels and weeping willows carved into their surfaces. A thick layer of algae coats every surface, slicking the stones and obscuring what little detail remains visible. The stench of decay hangs heavy in the air-a combination of rotting wood, stagnant water, and something else indefinable.

77638.description: Twisted willow branches claw at the grey sky overhead, dripping stagnant water onto the murky ground. A network of crumbling stone markers leans precariously amongst the exposed roots of ancient trees. Thick moss carpets many of the stones, obscuring faded carvings and blurring what little remains of their inscriptions. The air hangs heavy with the scent of decay and damp earth, a cloying sweetness barely masked by something acrid. Several wooden crosses lie splintered in the mud; they were likely swept downriver long ago. A thick layer of peat covers most surfaces, sucking at boots with each step across the uneven ground. Piles of dead leaves gather in the hollows between the stones, forming small islands of dry matter within the mire. The distant rush of water suggests the river's relentless encroachment on this place.

77639.description: The stagnant water here reflects a sky choked with grey clouds and fading light. Weathered stones mark graves, their inscriptions blurred by decades of rain and moss growth. Twisted roots from long-dead trees claw up through cracks in the stone markers, as though trying to reclaim them. A thick layer of algae coats many of the headstones, making it difficult to discern any detail, while a sickly sweet odor rises from the fetid swamp. Sinking further into the murky water with each passing season, several larger stones have already disappeared completely. Fragments of broken pottery and rusted metal litter the ground between the graves; evidence of a hasty abandonment or failed restoration attempt. A few stunted willow saplings struggle to survive along the edge of the bog's black surface.

Cracked and moss-covered headstones jut from the waterlogged earth, many listing at unnatural angles or lying submerged entirely. A tangle of thorny vines covers a few of the larger markers, their crimson berries glistening in the dim light filtering through the dense canopy overhead. The air hangs heavy with the scent of decay - damp stone mingled with the sickly sweetness of rotting wood and stagnant water. Half-submerged iron fences mark what were once burial plots, now mostly collapsed or broken away. A scattering of rusted metal scraps lies amongst the graves, hinting at forgotten tools and grave markers long since stolen. Several gnarled tree roots have twisted their way through the stone foundations of some tombs, splitting them further.

Scattered remnants of funerary offerings - tarnished silver chains, fragments of painted wood - drift amongst the grave markers. Moss and algae cover much of the stonework, obscuring the faded carvings that once marked the dead. A thick layer of fallen leaves carpets the ground between the stones, occasionally disturbed by a slow movement beneath the surface. Twisted roots from long-dead trees clutch at some of the larger headstones, threatening to pull them into the mire. The air hangs heavy with the scent of decay and damp earth, mingling with the subtle sweetness of blooming swamp flowers. A rusted iron fence once enclosed this small cemetery but is now broken in several places and half submerged. Further stones mark out burial plots beyond those visible here, disappearing back into the encroaching swamp.

A pervasive odor hangs in the stagnant air - wet earth, decaying leaves, and something faintly acrid like old oil. Many of the stones are tilted at unnatural angles, half-submerged in black water reflecting the grey sky above. Twisted roots from nearby trees reach down into the cemetery, snagging on broken slabs and pushing up through flagstones. A large section of wrought iron fence lies collapsed along the northern edge, its intricate patterns obscured by algae growth. Rotting wooden coffins jut from the ground where the earth has subsided leaving gaps in the soil. Several small mounds appear to be recent accumulations of peat moss and debris around some of the older markers. The swamp water laps gently against the base of a large, leaning monument carved with faded imagery.

Thick curtains of Spanish moss hang from the gnarled branches of ancient oaks, obscuring many of the markers within. A thick layer of algae coats each stone that remains upright, making it difficult to read what inscriptions might linger beneath. The air carries a cloying sweetness as decay turns fallen leaves and blossoms into dark mulch on the water's surface. Fragments of marble lie half-submerged amongst clumps of reeds along the southern edge, hinting at once grander monuments now lost. A single raven perches atop one marker, its black feathers mirroring the stagnant water reflecting a sky obscured by hanging grey mist. The ground beneathfoot is spongy with wet leaves and rotted roots, sinking slightly with each step.

Stone markers jut from the mire, their inscriptions blurred by years of rain and encroaching moss. A rusted iron fence attempts to define the perimeter of this cemetery, though many posts have long since fallen into the bog. The ground is uneven underfoot, soft with decaying leaves and submerged debris; a persistent sucking sound accompanies each step. Thick vines twist around crumbling headstones, obscuring names and dates carved in grey stone. A scattering of wildflowers sprouts from within cracks in a collapsed crypt, their vibrant colors a stark contrast to the surrounding decay. The air hangs heavy with the scent of stagnant water and rotting wood.

A thick layer of silt covers the floor, disturbed here and there by the scuttling of unseen things beneath it. Moss clings to every surface; dampness permeates even the stonework itself. Faintly discernible carvings depicting long-forgotten rites are etched into several of the walls but are almost entirely obscured by the growth. A large stone sarcophagus dominates the centre of the chamber, its lid slightly ajar, revealing only darkness within. The scent of stagnant water mixes with an undertone of something older and more unpleasant-the smell of things long undisturbed.

89341.description: The forest floor is covered with carpets of moss and scrub, softening footfalls.  Strung between two thin trees, a large spider web covers the area.  Clusters of seasonal green flowers grow here beneath an arbor of branches, waiting to bloom.  A rotting carcass fouls the air with the acrid smell of death.  The snapping of tree branches echoes through the forest.  You can continue to the north, east and west.

95782.description: The surface of this enormous stump is slick with algae and moss, making footing treacherous. A thick layer of grey mold coats the exposed wood, smelling sharply of decay and stagnant water. Twisted vines crawl across the top, some bearing withered black berries, while others are choked with pale fungal growths. The air hangs heavy with the buzzing of unseen insects from within the stump's hollowed heart. Through gaps in the dense canopy above, a weak light illuminates patches of floating debris on the black water below. A rusted iron chain dangles forlornly from a rotted eye-bolt embedded near the edge. Several weathered stones lie scattered about the stump's top, hinting at some former structure now submerged within the mire.

95783.description: The river's surface here reflects the gray sky above with little ripple. A thick layer of algae coats the submerged roots that jut from the dark water, clinging to the wood like a green shroud. Several stumps, tall as buildings, rise from the shallow expanse, their tops lost in the mist hanging over the water. The stench of decay is strong here, mingled with the sharper scent of stagnant river water. A scattering of broken headstones lies partially submerged among the reeds along the southern edge; many are etched with names long since forgotten. Tangled masses of dark vines drape from the upper branches of the submerged trees like macabre decorations. A small pile of smooth stones sits upon a flat, moss-covered stump near the western bank.
